Thanks — quick legal summary after an initial review of the questionnaire and SOW:

- EU-only deployment: acceptable if the deployment is in customer-controlled network and we confirm zero cross-border backups; needs Ops runbook and a data flow diagram in the SOW.
- Customer-managed KMS: possible under a Special Hosting Addendum; we must limit key import/export procedures and accept indemnity language to protect Redwood.
- Quarterly on-site audits: atypical. We can allow audits but recommend remote audits first; on-site once annually unless there's a material incident. On-site quarterly increases operational risk and cost.
- 90-day audit-log retention: longer than our default 30 days. We can offer 90 days as a paid add-on.
- 20% discount: pricing must be routed through Deal Desk; any discount >15% requires VP approval.

If we proceed, I recommend: 1) sign-off for a 15% standard deal desk discount from Rishi, 2) approval for a one-time engineering mobilization fee to cover the air-gapped install, and 3) limited quarterly audit language: remote quarterly reviews + on-site within 60 days upon request (max once per year standard).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the concise summary. Decision below — I'm approving the requested exceptions with the following hard conditions: 

1) Discount: approve up to 18% for year 1 only, but only if the customer commits to a 24-month minimum term and a price step-up to list in year 2 (documented in the contract).
2) Mobilization credit: approve Redwood covering up to €35k (slightly below your ask). Any additional mobilization must be invoiced to Medicorp.
3) KMS / HSM: approve customer-managed KMS under Special Hosting Addendum. Security/engineering to run a joint key exchange runbook and a successful dry-run before production.
4) Audits/logs: decline quarterly on-site audits. Offer remote quarterly attestations and one on-site audit per year; 90-day log retention is allowed as a paid add-on (pricing as recommended). Redwood legal will require a reciprocal review period and controls evidence requirements; customer must sign an access-limited NDA for on-site visits.
5) Liability: do NOT modify standard liability cap beyond a narrow carveout for data breach tied to our gross negligence; any further liability concessions are not approved.

Please incorporate these bullets into a proposed SOW amendment and pricing table and get Medicorp to countersign. Marissa, take lead on the commercial presentation; Laura, finalize the Special Hosting Addendum language; Rishi, update deal/legal redlines and record approver/conditions in HubSpot.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales — Enterprise
